turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep spending money when I'm stressed. Like, retail therapy.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's very human. Shopping gives a quick little reward, which feels nice when everything else is hard.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, next thing. I want to track my sleep for a month, and I'm not sure which way to do it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The first one is— oh, sorry, don't comment until I've got through all of them.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wear a fitness watch to bed, which tracks heart rate and when I wake up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Use a free app that sits on the mattress and listens for movement and snoring.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or just keep a paper diary on my nightstand, writing bedtime and how rested I feel.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's the full list. Go ahead.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A simple diary plus the free app is a great combination for a month. The watch is nice if you already own one, but don't worry too much about its exact sleep stages.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: But then I feel worse when I see my bank account.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Right, the comfort doesn't last. One trick is a waiting rule. Leave things in your basket for two days before buying.
